title: The commonplace contract (the ABI)
summary: The single shape every room uses to keep a passage. Frozen in 'The Canon OS — whole-ecosystem architecture (2026-07-21)' §Refactors 1; transcribed here from the behaviour of armarium/pipeline/syntopicon.py so consumers can validate against an artifact instead of a paragraph.

filing.note: The importer globs ONLY these three folders under the vault's Syntopicon directory. A commonplace note filed anywhere else is invisible to the engine.

note.description: Why it struck you. PRIVATE — the export withholds this; it never leaves the machine.

source.description: The citation as free text — NOT a category word. The resolver concatenates source + loc and pattern-matches the result, so this field must carry the real reference.
source.why_bad: Category words carry no information the resolver can match; such an entry falls through to 'external' and never links to a live unit. This is exactly the drift the Florilegium shipped with on 2026-07-25 and corrected on 2026-07-26.
source.taxonomy_note: The Canon OS note's '(GBWW | EXT key | canonical | unit id)' describes the four KINDS of address you might write here. It is a taxonomy, not an enum of allowed strings.

loc.description: The address within whatever scheme `source` names.

ideas.description: Great-idea NUMBERS, keyed to syn_topics.number. The importer runs re.findall(r'\d+', ideas) — digits only.
ideas.warning: Free-text tags ('mind', 'liberty') contain no digits, yield zero ideas, and the entry is SILENTLY DROPPED from the Syntopicon. Fail-quiet: validate before writing.

share.description: Tier gate. true = the shareable layer may carry it into the public export; false = stays on the machine. Read as fm.get('share').lower() == 'true'.

display_fields.comment: Not part of the resolver contract; carried for human rendering in rooms that show a roster or a card.
display_fields.author: string

derived_fields.comment: COMPUTED by resolve(source, loc). Never authored by hand — a room that writes these is wrong.

unit_id.description: The corpus unit this passage resolves to, when it resolves.

rules: matches /\bgbww\b|\bsyntopicon\b/i  →  'adler_pointer' (never resolved, never transcribed; rendered as 'look it up in your set'. THIS IS THE IP GUARDRAIL.)
resolves against a live unit in the corpus  →  'resolved'
canonical scripture anywhere in source/loc  →  'resolved' as kjv:OSIS

invariants: No Adler pointer ever carries a resolved unit (pointer-not-copy).
The export withholds private prose (note, and anything with share=false).
ideas must survive as digits, or the entry does not exist to the engine.
round_trip_test: Room entry → rendered vault note → parse_commonplace → resolve → assert a live unit_id. One test guards every consumer; add it to armarium/tests/.
